answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies relies on each identity carrying a real, non-transferable cost that scales with how many identities an attacker makes. One is a per-identity bond locked in a native token and slashed on misbehavior: to register a key an operator must post capital. An attacker wanting N fake agents must post N bonds, so a swarm's cost grows linearly while one honest agent pays once. Reputation stays tied to the bond, so a ripple of clones cannot inherit trust. A grove of correlated keys voting alike gets flagged and slashed in bulk. At the nadir the swarm cannot pay.
